subject: Migration mode selection - deployment mode follow-up (Lumina Labs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@lumina.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@lumina.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Migration mode selection - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the call today, really helpful to understand Lumina's stack and priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

Recap of current state you shared:
- Production calling OpenAI for majority of traffic; stable but cost is growing and latency varies across regions.
- Small self-hosted cluster for special workloads (legacy GPU nodes) that you want to phase out due to maintenance overhead.
- Requirements: p99 generation latency <120ms for key routes, predictable throughput during peak ETL windows, SOC 2 evidence for procurement, and EU data residency for some customer segments.

Deployment options we discussed (high-level):
1) Hosted API - fastest to ramp (no infra to manage), ideal for quick PoC and early production. Good if you prioritize time-to-value and want us to handle infra/ops.
2) Dedicated capacity - reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation. Strong fit if you need steady p99 latency and committed SLOs; supports autoscaling and burst policies.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) - customer-controlled networking and KMS/HSM options for regulated data; best for strict residency or air-gapped requirements.

Initial recommendation based on today's discovery: run a short PoC on Dedicated capacity for the most critical routes (gives predictable latency and easier migration off the legacy cluster), while keeping non-critical traffic on Hosted to reduce upfront commit. If residency or air-gap becomes a blocker, we can evaluate Private VPC for that subset.

Immediate next steps:
- I'll loop in Vivek for a technical deep-dive to map traffic patterns, sequence lengths, and KV cache opportunities (helps size Dedicated pool).
- I've attached our Dedicated pricing sheet and SOC 2 attestation for procurement.
- Can you share: (a) top 3 endpoints you want to migrate, (b) sample qps and token distribution, and (c) any specific compliance controls required?
- Proposed time for deep-dive: Tue 20 Apr 10:00-11:00 PT - does that work?

Attachments: Redwood-Dedicated-pricing-APR2027.pdf, SOC2-Attestation-2026.pdf

Thanks - happy to iterate.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex@lumina.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@lumina.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration mode selection - post-call recap & next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear summary - that matches our take. A few clarifying Qs from our side:
1) For Dedicated, what's the typical contract term and minimum commit? We prefer 12-18 month terms but want flexibility for scaling.
2) For data residency: we have EU customer data that must not leave EU. Would Dedicated in a US region be acceptable if we route EU customers to a Hosted EU region, or do we need a Private/VPC to guarantee residency?
3) For migration: can we do a phased cutover per endpoint? One concern is keeping failover to our legacy cluster during the rollout.

Also looping Emma from procurement - Emma, could you confirm the procurement contact/PO cadence and if you need the SOC2 evidence up front?

Alex
Head of ML Engineering | Lumina Labs
alex@lumina.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@lumina.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@lumina.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migration mode selection - post-call recap & next steps

Alex - great questions, answers inline below.

1) Contract term / commit: Dedicated typically has 6/12/24 month commits. Minimum commit for guaranteed SLA starts at the 3-GPU equivalent baseline; we can size based on your qps distribution and then offer a staged ramp. We can be flexible on term if you prefer a pilot + conversion path - I'll include options in the pricing PDF.

2) Data residency: If EU residency is required for specific customer data, the safest path is to provision Dedicated capacity in an EU region or use Private VPC with customer-managed networking. Hosted EU region can be used for EU-only traffic, but if you need strict contractual guarantees and customer-managed networking (e.g., for EU-only HSM), Private VPC is more appropriate. We'll cover tradeoffs in the deep-dive.

3) Phased cutover: absolutely - phased per endpoint is standard. We support routing policies and can keep the legacy cluster as a fallback during rollout; we'll want to capture failover criteria and traffic steering rules in the mutual action plan.

Vivek / Neha - can you join the deep-dive on Tue 20 Apr at 10:00 PT? Vivek can lead the architecture/traffic sizing; Neha can handle compliance questions if procurement wants to review controls. I've attached SOC2 and pricing again for reference.

Thanks - I'll send a calendar invite and a draft mutual action plan prior to the call.

Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Marissa,

Draft agenda for Tue deep-dive (15-30m):

- 10m: Sizing recommendations for Dedicated + autoscaling considerations
- 5m: Residency & security controls (Neha to confirm SOC2 scope / KMS options)

I've started a mutual-action-plan template and attached it (mutual-action-plan-lumina.xlsx). I'll also prepare an initial Dedicated sizing estimate based on the numbers Alex provides.

Vivek
